chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the earnings of the female singers, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which men enter upon her for is prohibited, and that which she is invited to the weddings, there is no problem with it.'
And it is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from the way of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the earnings of female singers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the permissibility of female singers' earnings by distinguishing between private performances for men, which are prohibited due to potential fitnah, and public wedding invitations, which are permissible. This ruling is grounded in the Quranic concept of 'lahw al-hadith' (Surah Luqman 31:6), interpreted by Shia scholars as music or discourse that distracts from divine guidance, with the context determining whether the distraction is significant enough to render the earnings haram.
